title: Diffusive row-total-variation decay and averaged mixing bound for finite lazy chains of nonnegative intrinsic directed curvature
difficulty_reason: For the intrinsic directed distance induced by the finite transition support, a coupling distance may have arbitrarily large upward increments as the state space varies. After ordinary finite optimal-transport existence, four-corner mass exchange, exponential stopping and L1-Cheeger steps are deducted, the authored burden is to match a doubly optimal coupling with at least p_min probability of decreasing the integer distance to a hitting-time tail requiring only a non-stagnation probability, thereby recovering diffusive row-total-variation decay without a uniform increment bound. The averaged displacement/conductance mixing estimate then uses this same mechanism by summing the transition-row observable; it is not a second independent H2 or an H3.
